title: The Nod (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist social observation
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The nod is a form of communication between men in particular
That conveys everything necessary in the most perpendicular
To language way available — one downward tilt of the head
Means hello, acknowledgement, respect, and how've you been said

[Pre-Chorus]
I've been nodding at men on the street since my mid-twenties
And I have never had a conversation about the twenties

[Chorus]
The nod knows something I don't know
It knows the shortest distance between two men and the show
The nod carries the information without the words
It says I see you and that's sufficient — say the birds
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There is a hierarchy of nods and each has different meaning
The chin-up nod is casual and the chin-down nod is leaning
Toward respect — the single slow nod means we have agreed
The double fast nod means you heard what was said indeed

[Bridge]
In Zimbabwe the greeting was longer and more deliberate
A whole sequence involving hands that had its own literate
Language of connection — hello was not one nod
It was a conversation with the hands and that was not odd

[Outro]
The nod knows… eye contact plus tilt equals connection… nod knows
That's my boy
